strings.name: Ed Bastian
strings.role: Chief Executive Officer of Delta Air Lines
strings.summary: Ed Bastian is an American airline executive with an early career in auditing and finance. He joined Delta in 1998, returned after a brief departure in 2005 and became CEO in 2016. His tenure encompasses international airline partnerships, passenger service and recovery from major flight disruptions.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. The birth date comes from secondary material. Company statements are attributed positions; closure of an investigation does not mean all related litigation has ended.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Delta Air Lines and participates in global airline networks, passenger service and large-airline management.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from St. Bonaventure University in 1979 with a Bachelor of Business Administration.
strings.facts.f2.label: Early career
strings.facts.f2.value: Was an audit partner at Price Waterhouse and held financial management roles in PepsiCo businesses.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Employee-first philosophy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Delta’s official biography describes putting employees first as his management philosophy; this is the company’s account of its approach.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Passenger service after disruption
strings.highlights.h2.text: Publicly apologized after the 2024 flight disruption and outlined passenger assistance; subsequent regulatory findings and customer experience warrant separate assessment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Opposed Heathrow terminal change
strings.timeline.t1.text: As CEO, opposed the decision to relocate Delta from Terminal 3 to Terminal 4; the statement does not establish that the move had occurred.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Regulatory investigation closure reported
strings.timeline.t2.text: Reuters reported that the US Department of Transportation confirmed it had closed its investigation into the 2024 disruption without seeking penalties, while still directing adequate customer service.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Apologized for flight disruption
strings.timeline.t3.text: Apologized to passengers following disruption triggered by the CrowdStrike outage; normal operations were still a forecast at that point.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became Chief Executive Officer
strings.timeline.t4.text: Succeeded Richard Anderson as CEO; the appointment had been announced on February 3 that year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Promoted to President
strings.timeline.t5.text: After serving as finance chief, became President of Delta Air Lines.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Returned to Delta as CFO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Had left Delta early in the year to become finance chief at Acuity Brands, then returned to Delta in July.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Delta Air Lines
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined as Vice President of Finance and Controller, continuing his financial management career.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned bachelor’s degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from St. Bonaventure University with a Bachelor of Business Administration.
